messages.author: Maria Chait
messages.title: UCL Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Auditory Neuroscience
messages.body_html:
Postdoctoral Research Fellow – Auditory Cognitive Neuroscience
UCL Ear Institute | Grade 7 | 36 months | UKRI-funded

 

I am recruiting a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join my group at the UCL Ear Institute as part of a new UKRI-funded project investigating the human "auditory buffer".

The project aims to understand how the brain retains and uses recent auditory information to support perception, detect regularities and predict incoming sounds. We will investigate the capacity and limitations of this auditory memory system, the neural and computational mechanisms that underpin it, and how its function varies across individuals and age groups.

 

The research combines large-scale behavioural experiments, EEG and MEG recordings, pupillometry and computational modelling, offering an exciting opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of auditory neuroscience, cognitive neuroscience and computational approaches to perception. The successful candidate will join a vibrant community of systems and cognitive neuroscientists at UCL, benefiting from a stimulating, interdisciplinary and collaborative research environment.

 

We are seeking a motivated researcher with a PhD in neuroscience or a related discipline (e.g. biology, biomedicine or experimental psychology), a strong academic background and a proven track record of research.

Essential expertise includes experience in cognitive neuroscience research, strong programming and signal-processing skills, and experience in analysing and/or computationally modelling neuroimaging data (EEG, MEG and/or fMRI).

The position offers substantial opportunities for intellectual contribution, methodological innovation and professional development.

 

Vacancy details and application link: : https://www.ucl.ac.uk/about/work-at-ucl/search-jobs/details?nPostingId=20263&nPostingTargetId=49739&id=Q1KFK026203F3VBQBLO8M8M07&LG=UK&languageSelect=UK&mask=ext

Application deadline: 16 November 2026.

Enquiries : Maria Chait EMAIL_REDACTED

 

Please do circulate the opportunity below to wider networks.

Many thanks!

Maria

 

%%

topics.snippet: Dear colleagues, The Department of Psychology at Tulane University is recruiting a tenure-track

messages.author: EMAIL_REDACTED
messages.title: Tenure-Track Faculty Position in Behavioral Neuroscience at Tulane University
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

The Department of Psychology at Tulane University is recruiting a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Behavioral Neuroscience, and I am chairing the search committee.

We are conducting a broad search and are particularly interested in candidates whose research examines how social and biological contexts shape behavior, including research related to lifespan development and resilience. We welcome applicants using a wide range of approaches in behavioral and systems neuroscience.

The full consideration deadline is December 1, 2026, with an anticipated start date of July 1, 2027.

The full job posting and application instructions are available here:

https://tulane-ibqejb.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1001/job/2208

Please share this opportunity with anyone who might be interested. I would be happy to answer questions about the position.

Best,

Jonathan Fadok
Tulane University

messages.title: Recruiting Ph.D students in computational cognitive neuroscience
messages.body_html:
I am looking for a Ph.D student interested in using computational approaches, behavioral methods and/or neuroimaging to study one or more of the following areas:

1. Recognition of objects, actions and events
2. Multi-task learning
3. Agent understanding
4. Individual variation in autism and other psychiatric disorders

The laboratory collaborates with Computer Science and Physics PIs, offering opportunities for interdisciplinary training. The position starts in Fall 2027, the deadline for applications is December 15, 2026. For inquiries please contact EMAIL_REDACTED sending a CV and a brief statement of skills and research interests.

Stefano Anzellotti (he/him)
Associate Professor, Department of Psychology and Neuroscience
Chair, Research Computing Committee
Boston College
https://sccnlab.bc.edu/

topics.title: Postdoc & PhD student positions at the University of Rochester
topics.snippet: Postdoctoral and graduate student positions available How does the brain infer causal relationships

messages.author: Ralf Haefner
messages.title: Postdoc & PhD student positions at the University of Rochester
messages.body_html:
Postdoctoral and graduate student positions available

How does the brain infer causal relationships in the world? How do beliefs about the causal structure of a scene influence motion perception? How can the underlying computations be modeled using Bayesian inference, and how can these computations be tested using neurophysiological experiments?

For this collaborative project between the computational neuroscience lab of Dr. Ralf Haefner, and the neurophysiology lab of Dr. Gregory DeAngelis, both at the Department of Brain & Cognitive Sciences at the University of Rochester, we are looking to recruit two postdoctoral fellows and PhD students. This project is highly collaborative with all researchers being involved in most aspects of the project from experimental design to data collection to data analysis & theory development. The project is based on our prior collaborative work [1,2] and we will have two related posters at the upcoming SfN meeting [3,4].

For the theoretical/computational efforts, candidates are expected to have a background in a quantitative field like computational neuroscience, machine learning, math & psychology, etc.. For the experimental efforts, candidates are expected to have a background in neuroscience, experimental psychology, biomedical engineering, or a related field, and previous research experience in systems neuroscience is highly beneficial. If interested, please submit your CV, a statement of research interests, and the names and contact information for three references to EMAIL_REDACTED or EMAIL_REDACTED. Ralf will also be at SfN to answer any questions.

The UR/BCS department is at the center of a vibrant and supportive scientific community. It has particularly strong ties to the Center of Visual Science, the Department for Neuroscience, the Department for Computer Science, the Department for Linguistics, and the Data Science Institute.

Rochester in upstate NY is family-friendly and affords a high quality of life with access to a world-class symphony, museums, and a wide range of outdoor activities: several parks within cycling distance, 20min by car to sandy beaches on Lake Ontario, 1h to Finger Lakes / wine country / skiing, 3h to great hiking in the Adirondacks. We also have a balanced 4 season climate with weather for every occasion: Lilac Festival in the spring, beautiful sunny summers (<10 days above 90 degrees), gorgeous fall foliage, and guaranteed snow in the winter. More info here: https://www.visitrochester.com.

[1] Shivkumar, S., DeAngelis, G. C., & Haefner, R. M. (2025). Hierarchical motion perception as causal inference. Nature Communications, 16(1), 3868.
[2] Lengyel, G., Shivkumar, S., DeAngelis, G. C., & Haefner, R. M. (2026). Bayesian causal inference unifies perceptual and neuronal processing of center-surround motion in area MT. eLife. https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.110621.1
[3] Dong et al. (2026). Neural correlates of speed-dependent relative motion perception in area MT. SfN Poster# PSTR184.01 / AA2, WCC Halls A-C, Nov 16, 1-5pm
[4] Yuan et al. (2026). Motion perception as causal inference: testing the causality assumption. SfN Poster# PSTR184.02 / AA3, WCC Halls A-C, Nov 16, 1-5pm

topics.title: Open-Rank Faculty Positions in Computational Mind & Behavior | Vanderbilt University
topics.snippet: Dear colleagues We're hiring at Vanderbilt! Join us in building Computational Mind & Behavior

messages.author: Rachael Jack
messages.title: Open-Rank Faculty Positions in Computational Mind & Behavior | Vanderbilt University
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues

We're hiring at Vanderbilt!  Join us in building Computational Mind & Behavior.

We use computation to make mind and behavior explainable—and mind and behavior to make new forms of computation possible.

At Vanderbilt University's College of Connected Computing, we're building Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB) around this two-way scientific ambition. We're recruiting exceptional scholars at Assistant, Associate, and Full Professor levels to help shape our scientific directions, collaborations, and intellectual community.

Our vision is to discover the principles that generate intelligence and behavior—from brains and individuals to interacting agents, groups, cultures, and societies—and understand what happens as human and artificial intelligence become increasingly intertwined.

We're particularly interested in four interconnected research directions:
🧠 Brain & Cognition / NeuroAI — How biological and artificial systems perceive, learn, reason, decide, and adapt.
💬 Language, Embodiment & Interaction — How minds communicate and connect through language, multimodal signals, embodied behavior, and human–AI interaction.
🤝 Strategic Social Behavior — How cooperation, competition, social inference, and strategic decision-making emerge among interacting agents.
🌐 Networks & Collective Intelligence — How behavior and intelligence emerge across social networks, cultures, populations, and human–AI collectives.

We welcome outstanding researchers from computing, AI, psychology, cognitive science, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We value deep disciplinary expertise, ambitious scientific questions, innovative computational approaches, and the potential to forge new connections across fields.

Join us in building an intellectual community that connects fundamental discoveries about intelligence and behavior with new computational ideas, methods, and technologies.

Interested in joining us?
We'd be delighted to hear from prospective candidates and discuss our scientific vision, recruitment priorities, and opportunities within CMB.

Contact
Prof. Rachael E. Jack
Area Head, Computational Mind & Behavior
EMAIL_REDACTED

How to apply
Application links:
Assistant Professor: https://lnkd.in/eWVhNVtY
Associate & Full Professor: https://lnkd.in/edtYbiym

In Interfolio, select “Humans, Computing and Society” as your primary review area; identify a secondary review area, if applicable (e.g., Physical Intelligence). In your cover letter, explicitly state your interest in Computational Mind & Behavior (CMB).

Explore our scientific vision: https://lnkd.in/eW3YVmev

Full consideration deadline: December 1, 2026.

Please share widely with colleagues and potential candidates!


Prof. Rachael E. Jack, Ph.D.
Professor of Computational Social Cognition
Professor of Psychology
Area Lead: Computational Mind & Behavior
Co-Director: MOSAIC
Past-President | Society for Affective Science
Editor-in-Chief | Advances in Psychological Science Open
College of Connected Computing
Vanderbilt University
Nashville, Tennessee, USA

messages.body_html:
6th Applied Active Inference Symposium · November 12–13, 2026 (online and free)

Join us for an exploration of Active Inference across domains and scales! This online and free event welcomes participants from all backgrounds, featuring 57 presentations, including a keynote and panel with Karl Friston, by: Adam Safron, Ahmad Nazzal, Alexander Sabine, Alison Gopnik, Andrew Pashea, Anna Pereira, Avel Guénin—Carlut, Bianca Avanzo, Bo Lee, Bradly Alicea, Bruce Tisler, Cleber Gomes, Colin Turfus, Dan Corva, Daniel Dragolich, Daniel Friedman, Diaconescu Adrian-Stelian, Ed Ober, Glen EP Ropella, Harshil Shah, Holly Grimm, Hongju Pae, Hyojun Choi, Jean-François Cloutier, John Boik, John H. Clippinger, Karl Friston, Kevin Backhouse, Lancelot Da Costa, Luca Possati, Majid D. Beni, Matthew Brown, Michael Lennon, Michael Walker, Mike Levin, Montijn van Loo, Nick Hay, Patricia Craja, Paulo Santiago, Rajkaushik Borgohain, Robert Worden, Ryan Smith, Satyaki Maitra, Sergio Rubin, Sheena Yap Chan, Stell, Steph Macurdy, Takuya Isomura, Tao Gong, Ted J. Vrioni, Tiga Kailimai, Tran Hoang Linh, Viraj Deshwal, Vitalii Shapovalov, Vitória de Souza, Xin Sun.

Highlights:
  • Two days of livestreamed talks, panels and working-group sessions (12:00–22:00 UTC each day), plus 40 prerecorded presentations
  • Interactive sessions: hands-on workshops, including a code-along cpomdp session (“Build a curious rocket”), a modular perspective layer for active inference agents, and an in-depth discussion on world models in natural and artificial intelligence
  • Connecting with useful materials (educational, code and more) and with people who are learning and applying Active Inference
Register now (free): https://registersymposium2026.activeinference.institute/
Program and more information: https://2026symposium.activeinference.institute/
Watch the livestreams (YouTube playlist): https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLO2noumu0LRk

Full announcement: https://activeinferenceinstitute.substack.com/p/next-week-6th-applied-active-inference

messages.author: Lucas Tian
messages.title: Ph.D. and Postdoc positions (Tian lab at NYU)
messages.body_html:
*The Tian Laboratory of Cognitive Neural Systems is opening at New York University on January 2027*

The Tian Lab, based in NYU’s Center for Neural Science, has fully funded openings for Ph.D. students and postdocs to lead projects studying the neural basis of intelligence—focusing on how neural systems learn and generalize by representing the world's abstract, compositional structure and reorganizing it to solve novel problems, in the context of rich motor and cognitive tasks.
 
The successful candidate will join a multidisciplinary team (including neuroscientists, cognitive scientists, and engineers) and lead a project involving one or more of the following approaches: (1) Behavior and electrophysiology in animal models; (2) Computational modeling of behavior and neural activity; (3) Behavior and neural recordings in humans. 

Postdoc applicants: See https://apply.interfolio.com/195790

Ph.D. applicants: Apply through an appropriate NYU Ph.D. program. Either: (1) Apply to the NYU Neural Science Doctoral Program and mention Lucas as a potential mentor; (2) Apply directly to Lucas through the NYU Tandon Biomedical Engineering Ph.D. program. 


--------------------------------------------
Lucas Y. Tian, PhD
(Starting January 2027)
Assistant Professor of Neural Science and Biomedical Engineering
New York University

https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/lucas-tian.html

messages.title: Many Funded Ph.D. Positions at the International Max Planck Research School for Intelligent Systems (IMPRS-IS)
messages.body_html:
The Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and the Universities of Stuttgart and Tübingen collaborate to offer an interdisciplinary doctoral program, the International Max Planck Research School for Intelligent Systems (IMPRS-IS). This doctoral program will accept its 11th generation of doctoral researchers in 2027.

This school is a key element of Baden-Württemberg’s Cyber Valley initiative to accelerate basic research and commercial development in artificial intelligence and robotics. We seek students who want to earn a doctorate while contributing to world-leading research in areas such as:

•  Artificial Intelligence
•  Biomedical Technology
•  Computational Cognitive Science
•  Computer Vision and Graphics
•  Control Systems and Optimization
•  Data Science
•  Haptics and Human-Computer Interaction
•  Machine Learning
•  Micro- and Nano-Robotics
•  Natural Language Processing
•  Neuroscience
•  Perceptual Inference
•  Robotics and Human-Robot Interaction
•  Soft Robotics and Materials

Our renowned faculty include Sahar Abdelnabi, Rediet Abebe, Amirreza Aghakhani, Aamir Ahmad, Buse Aktaş, Frank Allgöwer, Maksym Andriushchenko, Kai Arras, Julian Berberich, Philipp Berens, Matthias Bethge, Wieland Brendel, Andrés Bruhn, Andreas Bulling, Martin Butz, Manfred Claassen, Alberto Comoretto, Maximilian Dax, Stephan Eckstein, Benedikt Ehinger, Carsten Eickhoff, Veronika Eyring, Peter Gehler, Andreas Geiger, Jonas Geiping, Antonia Georgopoulou, Martin A. Intelligent systems that can successfully perceive, act, and learn in complex environments hold great potential for aiding society. We seek doctoral students who are curious, creative, and passionate about research to join our school and help advance human knowledge about intelligent systems.

• Admitted students can join our program starting in spring of 2027.
• You will be mentored by our internationally renowned faculty.
• You will register as a university doctoral student and conduct research.
• IMPRS-IS offers a wide variety of scientific seminars, workshops, and social activities.
• All aspects of our program are in English.
• Your doctoral degree will be conferred when you successfully complete your doctoral project.
• Our dedicated staff members will assist you throughout your time as a doctoral student.

People with a strong academic background and a master’s degree (conferred or expected soon) in Engineering, Computer Science, Cognitive Science, Mathematics, Control Theory, Neuroscience, Materials Science, Physics, or related fields should apply.

topics.title: Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence (SUSHI) Symposium 2027
topics.snippet: Dear Colleagues, We wish to invite you to attend the SUSHI (Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence

messages.author: Daniel Bush
messages.title: Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence (SUSHI) Symposium 2027
messages.body_html:
Dear Colleagues,

We wish to invite you to attend the SUSHI (Single Unit Studies of Human Intelligence) symposium, a two-day satellite event taking place in Glasgow immediately before the 7th International Conference on Memory (ICOM-7) next year.

SUSHI will bring together leading laboratories using human intracranial single-neuron recordings to investigate learning, memory, and higher-order cognition. The symposium is intended as a focused forum for discussing recent advances, emerging methods, and future directions in the study of human single-neuron activity.

The programme will consist exclusively of short talks from leading researchers in the field, designed to maximise scientific exchange and discussion.

The symposium will be organised around two broad themes:
Day 1 - Episodic memory, spatial cognition, and the hippocampus
Day 2 - Speech and language, auditory cognition, and the neocortex

For those interested in only one of these themes, single-day registration options will be available.

We hope that SUSHI will provide a unique opportunity for researchers working with human single-unit recordings to exchange ideas in an intimate setting before joining the broader memory science community at ICOM-7.

Further details, including registration information and the scientific programme, can be found on the symposium website here. You can sign up to receive further updates via the mailing list here.

We would be delighted if you could join us in Glasgow, and grateful if you could share this invitation with any interested parties.

With best wishes,

Daniel Bush & Simon Hanslmayr
On behalf of the SUSHI 2027 Organising Committee

----------------------------------------------------

Dr. Daniel Bush

GM01, Medical Sciences Building, Gower Street, London, WC1E 6BT

Associate Professor, UCL Department of Neuroscience, Physiology and Pharmacology

Principal Investigator, UCL Human Electrophysiology Lab

Co-director, UCL Centre for Neuro-AI

Section Editor, PLoS Computational Biology

topics.title: Postdoctoral Researcher – Developing Cortical Networks at UMN
topics.snippet: Postdoctoral Researcher – In Vivo Imaging and Electrophysiology of Developing Cortical Networks Smith

messages.author: Gordon Smith
messages.title: Postdoctoral Researcher – Developing Cortical Networks at UMN
messages.body_html:
Postdoctoral Researcher – In Vivo Imaging and Electrophysiology of Developing Cortical Networks

Smith Lab – University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN


Before the cortex can process sensory information, its circuits must first organize themselves. The Smith Lab at the University of Minnesota studies how this happens. We have found that distributed, modular networks with millimeter-scale correlations exist throughout the developing neocortex, and using in vivo optogenetics and computational modeling, we have shown that these networks are self-organizing and depend on local intracortical circuitry. We are now asking how early network activity shapes the circuits that emerge: by imaging, recording, and perturbing activity in vivo during development, and comparing the results against models of network self-organization.


The postdoc will lead projects combining two-photon imaging, optogenetics, and electrophysiology in the developing cortex, with the opportunity to shape the direction of their own work.

Recent work: Mulholland, et al. bioRxiv, 2026 ·  Powell, et al. PNAS 2024 · Lab website: smithneurolab.org

For more details, including how to apply please see:

https://www.smithneurolab.org/positions/postdoc-2026

Gordon Smith, Ph. D. 

Associate Professor
Associate Director of Graduate Studies 
Graduate Program of Neuroscience
Optical Imaging and Brain Science Medical Discovery Team
Department of Neuroscience
Center for Magnetic Resonance Research
University of Minnesota

topics.snippet: Dear colleagues, The Division of Basic Research in the Department of Anesthesiology at Washington

messages.author: Cheng, Wayland
messages.title: Open Rank Faculty Position in Basic Biomedical Research – WashU Medicine
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

The Division of Basic Research in the Department of Anesthesiology at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis is recruiting tenure track or tenured faculty.

Our open rank search welcomes outstanding scientists across all areas of basic biomedical research, including molecular and cellular biology, neuroscience, and related disciplines. We seek creative and innovative investigators who will bring new scientific directions and help shape the future of basic research in our highly collaborative environment. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

For additional information and to apply:
https://facultyopportunities.wustl.edu/Posting/Detail/1011265

Please share this opportunity with interested colleagues and trainees.

Thank you!
Wayland Cheng

messages.title: Post-Doc opening in NHP systems neuroscience Paris Brain Institute
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

We are currently recruiting a Postdoctoral Researcher in NHP systems neuroscience to join our team at the Paris Brain Institute (CNRS/Sorbonne Universite), in France. The project uses fMRI-guided neurophysiology to investigate multi-sensory social perception in monkeys and is funded by an ERC Grant (NEURO-SOCIETY).

Link to the position description and application: https://offres.institutducerveau-icm.org/fr/jobs/2021-23  
Enquiries: EMAIL_REDACTED   
Lab website: Neurophysiology of Social Cognition Lab.
Dates: Review of applications will continue until the position is filled

Please don't hesitate to distribute it to potentially interested candidates. 
Many thanks
Julia
